top_choice_rationale: P001 rewards a quantitative prediction (Bistritzer and MacDonald, 2011) of flat bands at a specific twist angle, followed by the experimental discovery of gate-tunable correlated insulating and superconducting states at that angle (Jarillo-Herrero and collaborators, 2018). The platform has been reproduced by many independent groups and extended to other moire systems, and its existence does not depend on the unresolved pairing mechanism, so a citation worded around the flat-band prediction and the observed phases is secure. Keeping Bistritzer preserves the joint 2011 prediction; the omission of Cao, Fatemi and others is a real cost that the record should state openly. P002 (Katori and Ye) is a sound, more finished and cleanly credited second choice, but it refines an established measurement tradition rather than opening a new regime. Any award is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: No profile-based conflict with the credited names in P001 or P002: I have no documented tie to MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer, Katori or Ye. Disclosed proximity only: I direct WACQT and work in superconducting circuits and quantum-computing theory, and Chalmers hosted researchers associated with the 2025 prize, none of which touches these proposals.
